tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-backend.md <<'EOF'
# TLS backend

The project's current recorded decision is to use Rustls as the TLS backend. It was chosen because it fits the project's Rust code better, has fewer CVEs, and is simpler.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-backend.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-backend.md`. It says the current recorded decision is Rustls, chosen because it fits the project's Rust code better, has fewer CVEs and is simpler. It doesn't mention the retired alternative.

Muninn flags a conflict on this decision. Both #21 (Rustls) and #7 (OpenSSL, "the standard for production TLS") are marked active, and nothing formally marks #7 as replaced. I went with Rustls because #21 is the later of the two user decisions (15:41 against 15:36 the same day). The assistant's acknowledgement at the time also said it replaced #7. If OpenSSL is meant to stand, the file needs changing, and it would help to record that explicitly.

I left out #31 (self-signed certificates for testing) and #30 (verification in all builds). They look related to TLS, but neither one names a backend.
